Not for redistribution without written consent of Morgan Stanley Morgan Stanley RESEARCH Idea December 2, 2025 11:45 PM GMT Amazon.com Inc | North America AWS re:Invent: Chips, Agents and More re:Invent '25 brought announcements from chips to agentic offerings. We remain constructive AWS's competitive positioning and growing suite of models, tools and apps to accelerate GenAI transformation and AWS growth. We are encouraged by expanding NVDA chip supply. Remain OW, PT $315 (~35% upside). AWS re:Invent 2025 brought multiple announcements from AWS from chips to agentic offerings...that we see driving continued digitization of enterprise workloads and better than expected AWS forward revenue growth. We now turn to analyzing six key announcements and our thoughts on what to watch next across each vector/ offering. NVDA Chip Availability: AWS highlighted its leading reliability/availability running NVDA GPUs (see Exhibit 1 ) and announced its latest P6e instances in EC2 powered by GB300 (NVDA's latest Blackwell Ultra GPUs). The company also spoke to examples of customers running workloads utilizing NVDA GPUs on AWS including...NVDA themselves (Project Ceiba cluster on AWS), OpenAI (using clusters of EC2 ultraservers with hundreds of thousands of GB200 chips and soon to be GB300) and HUMAIN (partnership for AI zone in Saudi Arabia utilizing NVDA GPUs on AWS). We believe it will remain important for AWS to offer leading chips that its customers are interested in utilizing as they start/expand AI related projects. For more on AMZN's expected step-up on GPU purchases in '26 please see here. commitment to the Trainium series. The company spoke to 1M+ Trainium chips deployed to date and the majority of inference on Bedrock being powered by Trainium (including Anthropic's latest Claude models). Further, AWS announced that Trn3 ultraservers (4x compute, 4x memory bandwidth, 5x tokens/MW) are now generally available (perhaps delays not as bad as feared) and that Trn4 (6x performance, 4x memory bandwidth, 2x memory capacity, scale up with NVlink Fusion and UAlink) is in-design (we expect GA announcement at re:Invent 2026). In our view, material adoption of Trainium beyond Anthropic and AMZN themselves remains an unknown to monitor. The good news is (as mentioned above) we believe AWS will have more supply of GPUs to drive growth.
Expanded Nova Suite of Models Including Nova Forge: AMZN announced a second generation of it's own family of foundational models (Nova) and notably, AMZN also announced Nova Forge. Nova Forge gives enterprises the capability to deploy models on bedrock that blend their proprietary data with an Amazon Nova model training data-set to produce models that understand both enterprise specific data and the Nova model's core training data. The company highlighted RDDT's use of Nova Forge to integrate its own proprietary data in pre-training, enabling a model that understood its community-specific knowledge to help meet its accuracy and cost efficiency targets for content moderation. AMZN does not get any credit from investors for success from its own suite of models, so building Nova, which currently has tens of thousands of customers, could pose material upside to estimates and multiple.

Idea
Expanding AgentCore Tools: Bedrock AgentCore now has 2mn+ SDK downloads and AMZN added new capabilities including Policy and Evaluations. We see agents as being material sources of internal productivity, and AgentCore enables companies to build/scale company and multi-task agents…which should drive more durable multi-year AWS growth.
AMZN-Built Agents: AMZN detailed two of its in-house designed agents for third parties, notably Amazon Quick and Connect AMZN Quick: consumer-like agent for employees to analyze data (analytics, deep research, report writing, etc) Connect: AMZN customer service agent…that now has a $1bn+ Revenue run-rate, with tens of thousands of customers. These tools speak to how AWS is building next-gen capabilities for companies to adopt in order to drive more durable digitization and AWS revenue growth. The $1bn+ run-rate for Connect is a notable use case that should scale ahead, in our view.

frontier agents with Kiro, autonomous agents, etc.) is also growing to compete in this early, but highly competitive AI-assisted coding space. Offering AI coding tools is becoming somewhat table-stakes, and differentiation of Kiro vs others (including Claude Code/Codex and multiple other start-ups' tools) will be important to driving success. The limited time 1 year free offering of Kiro (up to 100 seats) at the very least should drive some experimentation and we view the integration with Github as notable too.
Remain OW, $315 PT and What to Watch From Here: We remain constructive AWS's competitive positioning and growing suite of models, tools, applications, and services to accelerate GenAI transformation and AWS growth. We are also encouraged by the expanding NVDA chip supply. We have AWS's expected forward data center square footage growth (here) and demand backlog (here) that give us confidence in low to mid 20's year-on-year growth into '26 (and potentially '27) and see this growth in '26 driving revisions and (more notably) multiple expansion toward our $315 PT (~35% upside).
